propositions: The plan-review gate's LLM judge produces inconsistent decisions when re-run on the same finding, introducing noise into the Pass-2/Pass-3 vocabulary that downstream stories R3 and R5 depend on.
Section-order permutation of input plans can flip the gate verdict between PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE, violating the stability assumption for new order-exposed criteria like R3's container criterion.

Experiment A measures self-consistency by re-judging 50 findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort (R5's routing cohort) 3 times each and computing Fleiss kappa and raw agreement; must meet kappa≥0.6 AND raw_agreement≥0.8 to pass and unblock R5.

Experiment B measures order-shuffle stability by judging 14 plans (from committed corpus_sample.json with ≥3 top-level sections) under 3 distinct deterministic section-order permutations each, computing agreement on verdict; must meet kappa≥0.6 AND raw_agreement≥0.8 to pass or else record as R3 prerequisite failure.

Infra-INDETERMINATE verdicts (those with coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed flags) are excluded as execution failures and re-run; genuine judge-INDETERMINATE is retained as a valid category.

Per-finding self-consistency is measured via decision∈{block,advisory,dropped,indeterminate} from Pass-3; per-plan order-stability is measured via verdict∈{PASS,BLOCK,INDETERMINATE} from the public review_plan entrypoint.
